title: FHS Homecoming  Wrap
full_story:
The Flora High School homecoming week culminated Saturday night with the Crowning of the Homecoming King and Queen.

Earning the Homecoming Queen crown is Mya Sloan, while Kormik Massie was chosen as Homecoming King.  Other candidates for Queen were Marli Myers, Qynlin Brown, Danica Conklin and Rosalyn Stanford.  The other King Candidates were Guy Arnold, Rylan Billingsly, Kehlin Crawford, Brennan O’Donnell, and Kormik Massie. The retiring 2025 FHS Homecoming royalty were Queen Makenna Hackney and King Dulaney Bullard.  Following coronation students enjoyed the dance until 10 pm.

The remaining members of the Flora High School Homecoming Court included Junior Class attendants Morgan Irmen, Mylea Jones, Kennedy Zimmerman, Tyler Earnst, Braxton Oestrich, and Ashton Williams.  The Sophomores Class attendants were Vayda Kohn and Carson Smith.  The Freshmen Class Attendants were Halle Patridge and Sawyer Murbarger.

Homecoming activities this past week consisted of dress up days, the parade Wednesday night and bonfire and the Homecoming Football game Friday night where the Flora Wolves defeated the Eldorado Eagles by a score of 45 to 0.

title: NORTH CLAY SCHOOL BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The North Clay School Board met in regular session on Wednesday night.

The evening started with a public hearing on the fiscal year 27 budget.  The budget was adopted during the regular meeting.  Revenue for FY27 is estimated to be 9.7million, while estimated expenditures are $10.4 million.  Expenditures are more than overall revenues due to a one time building project costs approved in FY26 with the expenditures occurring in FY27.

New staff members at North Clay for the 26-27 school year were recognized.

Building and Grounds Committee member Barry Adair shared that information would be gathered for bids for a potential concession stand and restroom facility for the high school baseball field area.  Superintendent Keith Price shared information on new safety procedures present on campus this school year.

In personnel matters, North Clay board members hired Hollie McCluskey as a permanent sub, approved Kim Smith as a volunteer at the elementary/junior high school, approved Kathy Byers as a volunteer at the elementary/junior high school, approved Alex Boose as junior high school boys basketball assistant coach, and authorized the Administration to hire non-certified personnel, as needed.

title: FLORA HALLOWEEN PARADE
full_story:
Entry forms for the Flora Chamber of Commerce Halloween Parade on Saturday night, October 31st at 7:00 pm are now available.  There is no theme, so entrants can use their own creativity when planning the entry.  All entries to the parade must be registered with the Chamber in order to participate.  Please register at the chamber no later than Noon on Friday, October 30th.  The Chamber office is open on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday from 8 am to 5 pm.

The parade route will start at The Depot (State Street) and end at Christ Church (Olive Street).  Emergency vehicles will be allowed to sound their sirens during the parade.

Staging areas will be given the day you register and parade numbers will be given the day of the parade when you check in.  Location of your Staging Area will be based on the type of entry.  The Chamber is asking everyone to please be respectful of the staging areas and leave them in the same condition they were in upon arrival.  All entries must check in with the staging area volunteer in the brightly colored vest, to officially check in and verify the entry has their card number on their entry for judging.  Bands, queens, and political entries do not need parade cards but do need to check in with the stage volunteer.

Horses are to unload at the Price Less IGA at 6 pm with a mandatory police escort to the grass area of GSI beginning at 6:15.  If you miss the police escort you will not be permitted in the parade.

Handicap spectators may park at Southern Lumber Company (corner of E. North Ave & South Mill) and please use the south entrance closest to the tracks.

All entries are required to register.  A $10 late fee will be required by any unregistered participant if they register after than Noon on Friday, October 30th.  There will be absolutely no throwing of candy from vehicles or trailers/float, candy can be handed out or tossed if you are a walker on the sides of the street.  If an entry is caught throwing, they will be disqualified from judging.

Performance groups may stop at the judging stand and do a performance no longer than 90 seconds.  Any performance longer than 90 seconds will disqualify you from judging.

title: CLAY COUNTY TAX SALE
full_story:
Clay County, as Trustee, has completed their tax deed proceedings on real estate properties that were delinquent in 2022 and mobile homes that were delinquent for 2023 and prior real estate taxes.  The County, as Trustee, will now offer for sale the real estate and mobile homes obtained to the public through a sealed bid auction.

They will offer approximately 10 real estate items and 2 mobile home items through a sealed bid auction sale.  All sealed written bids must be in the Clay County Treasurer’s Office located in the Clay County Courthouse, at 111 Chestnut Street, in Louisville, no later than the close of business on Friday.  All online bids must be submitted via www. iltaxsalebids.com no later than the close of business on Friday.

The sale of these lots and mobile homes should be a major benefit to both the Taxing Districts and the neighboring property owners.  This sale will place the real estate and mobile homes into the hands of individuals who have an interest in owning them.  The County, as Trustee, hopes that these new owners will both maintain the property and the mobile homes and keep the taxes paid.  By eliminating abandoned properties, the appearance of the neighborhood should improve, and the value of adjoining properties should increase.

The required minimum bid on real estate is $844.00, and on mobile homes is $915.00.  All items will be sold to the highest sealed bid received on or before Friday.  Complete bidder’s packets and sale catalogs are now available at the Clay County Treasurer’s Office or online at www. iltaxsale.com.

For further sale information, contact the Auction Sale Department of the Clay County Tax Agent’s Office.  The telephone number is 1-800-248-2850 or 618-656-5744 or visit www.iltaxsale.com.  Office hours are 8:00 am and 5:00 pm Monday through Fridays.

title: SANTA SMILES APPLICATIONS
full_story:
Applications for Santa Smiles for this year will be available starting Thursday.

Applications can be picked up at the Clay City Village Hall, Xenia Village Hall, Louisville Village Hall, Louisville Banking Company, or Salt & Strings Butchery.  In Flora applications are available at the Flora City Hall, Flora Library, CEFS, and the office of Todd Fender at the Clay County Housing Authority.  The Clay County Health Department will give their applications to their clients.

Applications are due on November 1st and can be dropped off at the Clay City Village Hall, Louisville Village Hall, and Xenia City Hall.  In Flora Applications can be dropped off at the Clay County Housing authority night drop box.  Applications can also be mailed.

Santa Smiles will also have a Christmas Auction on Friday, October 23rd at 6 pm at the Xenia Community Center.  Santa Smiles is providing concessions at the auction.

Again, applications will be available on October 1st.  Last year Santa Smiles provided gifts to 523 kids, and 71 residents at Chestnut Corner Sheltered Care in Louisville.

title: JOHNSONVILLE RURITAN FALL HUNT
full_story:
The Johnsonville Ruritan Club will have their third annual adult Fall Egg Hunt Saturday.

The evening will start with a meal at 5 pm that will cost $10.  The menu is chicken and noodles, mashed potatoes, green beans, hot rolls and desserts.  There will be to-go containers available.  There will also be a 50/50 raffle.  Everyone is welcome to the meal.

Registration for the hunt starts at 6:30 pm and the hunt will start at dark, cost is $20 per ticket and the hunt is open to those 18 and older.  Adults are welcome to bring a flashlight so they can hunt in the dark throughout marked areas in Johnsonville for an allotted amount of time.  Participants will collect as many eggs as possible for a chance to win prizes.  Prizes are being donated by area businesses.

People who want to participate can buy their tickets for the hunt in advance at The Village Florist in Cisne or online at runsignup.com.

title: UNEMPLOYMENT
full_story:
There was little change in unemployment in South Central Illinois between July and August.

The Illinois Department of Employment security reports unemployment in Clay County was 3.6%, which was two tenths of a percent lower than July and 1.5% below a year earlier.   The number receiving unemployment benefits in Clay County decreased from 214 to 203.  The county’s workforce also grew by 12 people to 5,429.

The lowest unemployment in the region was in Jasper County, where the rate decreased one-tenth of a percent to 2.8%.  Effingham County, Marion County, and Richland Count’s rate remained unchanged.  Effingham’s rate was 2.9%, Marion County’s rate was 4.2% and Richland County’s rate was 3.4%.  The lowest unemployment rate in the state was in Monroe County at 2.5% and the highest was in Edwards County at 7%.

There were 500 fewer nonfarm jobs in the Centralia-Mt. Vernon labor market this August compared to last year according to the Department of Employment Security.  The biggest increase in jobs was in private education-health services up 400 and government up 75 jobs.  Jobs in construction, information and other services remained unchanged.  The biggest job losses were in professional-business services, down 300 jobs.  Trade-transportation and utilities was also down 300 jobs.  Manufacturing dropped 150 jobs, financial activities were down 100 jobs, leisure hospitality down 75 jobs and natural resources-mining dropped 25 jobs.

The Unemployment Rate in Illinois for August was 4.9% up 3 tenths of a percent from July.  The National Unemployment Rate was 4.3% down one tenth of a percent.

title: LIHEAP AVAILABLE
full_story:
CEFS Economic Opportunity Corp, administers the Energy Assistance Program in Clay, Christian, Effingham, Fayette, Montgomery, Moultrie and Shelby counties.  Funds are available to assist income-eligible households with natural gas, propane and/or electric bills and furnace assistance for inoperable heating systems.

The program begins taking applications this coming Thursday, for adults age 60 and over, individuals with a disability, families with children age 5 years and under, and households that are disconnected from their utilities, have a disconnection notice or have less than 25% in their propane tank.  All other income eligible households can apply on November 2nd.

Applications are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis through August 13th, of 2027, or when funding is exhausted.  Households that receive a one-time benefit may return during the program year for Reconnection Assistance or Furnace Assistance benefits, if needed.

The program expands eligibility this year.  Households that are customers of Ameren Illinois, Liberty Utilities, City of Flora, Village of Louisville, Village of Clay City or Shelby Electric must be at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines to receive a benefit from LIHEAP.

The monthly income guidelines are, one person can make up to $3,990 a month, two people $5,410, three can make up to $6,830, and four people can earn up to $8,250.

Households that are customers of all other utilities/energy vendors must be at or below 60% of the State Median Income to receive a benefit from LIHEAP.

The income guidelines for that are, one person can earn up to $3,441 a month, two people $4,500, three can make up to $5,558, and four people up to $6,617.

Visit online at cefseoc.org  or liheapillinois.com  for the income limits for households with 5 members and more.

The Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) offers one-time benefits to eligible homeowners and renters to help with energy bills and for reconnection of energy service.

Documentation you’ll need includes: Proof of gross income from all household members for the prior 30-day period beginning with the application date.  For new customers applying for LIHEAP, and/or for new household members of previous customers, needed items are: proof of Social Security numbers (SSN) for all household members.  Individuals without an SSN or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) can still apply and CEFS Outreach offices will advise accordingly.  A copy of current heat and electric bills issued within the last 30 days.  Cash assistance is available for renters who can provide their lease/rental agreement showing their heating costs are included in the rent.  Other documents may be needed based on your household situation.  For questions call the office.

For an appointment, call 618-662-4024 for the CEFS Clay County Outreach office at 835 West North Avenue in Flora.  They’re open Monday-Friday from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

They continue to take applications in person or by phone.  The required documentation may can be submitted in-person, via the mail or electronically.  Special accommodation is also available for those who are in need of the service.  Please contact your local CEFS Outreach office to make arrangements.

Income eligible LIHEAP customers of Ameren Illinois receive a monthly discount on their natural gas and/or electric bill through the Low-Income Discount Rates.  Visit powerbilldiscount.com  for more details.

title: CHRONIC WASTING DISEASE SAMPLING KITS
full_story:
Beginning with the fall 2026 deer hunting season, the Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) will offer voluntary mail-in sampling kits to hunters who want to collect lymph node samples from harvested deer for chronic wasting disease (CWD) testing.

Kits will be available on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last.  Hunters may request up to two kits at a time and additional kits if they harvest more deer. Hunters can request kits online or by contacting a local district wildlife biologist.

Each kit includes instructions for removing lymph node samples from harvested deer.  The kits and laboratory testing are provided free of charge.  Test results will be posted online when available, generally within two to four weeks.  Priority will be given to samples from counties with known CWD cases.

Hunters can check test results through IDNR’s CWD test results database.  Hunters whose deer test positive for CWD will receive a text or email notification from IDNR.  An IDNR wildlife biologist will contact hunters by phone only when the harvest location has not been confirmed following notification.

CWD is a fatal disease of the central nervous system that affects deer and elk.  It was first detected in Illinois in a suspect adult female deer from northwest Boone County in 2002.  Since then, IDNR has sampled 199,136 wild deer statewide, with 3,410 testing positive for CWD.  The disease has been detected in 28 counties in northern and central Illinois.

From July 1st, 2025, through June 30th, 2026, IDNR identified 662 CWD-positive deer in 28 Illinois counties.  Reports are available online.

For more information about CWD surveillance visit IDNR’s CWD information page or contact Chris Jacques, Wildlife Disease Program manager, at [email protected].
